conviction_note: A Q3 trading update from a Bermuda reinsurer after a quarter that peers (Lancashire, Hiscox) and Gallagher Re have already called benign. The one company-specific new line is that the buyback restarts, which Conduit did in exactly the same words a year ago, with about $45.6m (about 5% of market cap) left on the programme. Against it: weaker investment marks, softening rates, and possible growth in Middle East political-violence losses. The findings net to +0.5. The scaled number is a mild lean, p_up 58 x abs 4.0 = +0.64. The two measurements agree in sign and are close in size because no single finding is decisive and the bar is unsourced.

bar: unsourced: Yahoo returns no consensus for CRE.L (baseline consensus.quarters empty, analyst_count null), and Conduit gives no numeric 2026 guidance, so every finding is capped small. The qualitative bar is the 2026-09-08 'in line with expectations' statement and peers' benign Q3.

findings.finding: Conduit's share count has been frozen since 25 June 2026: 155,754,560 voting rights at 30 Jun and the same base in FIL's 29 Sep TR-1. That is the same hurricane-season pause it took in 2025 and lifted in its Q3 2025 update, and about $45.6m is left on the current $50m programme ($38.9m bought in H1 minus $34.5m from the old programme = $4.4m used). So a restart worth about 5% of market cap is the most likely capital line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 update (5 Nov 2025), which announced the buyback restart after a benign Q3: +2.91% on the day (baseline history). Buyback announcement with Q1 2026 update: +2.14%.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody aggregates the halted share count. The weekly 'Transaction in own shares' RNS stopped after 30 Jun 2026, and the remaining capacity is only visible by subtracting figures across the prelims, the interims and the 26 May RNS. The stock trades at about 0.78x June TNAV (442.5p vs GBP 5.70), and the Lancashire special-dividend day (+2.7% in CRE on 4 Nov) faded back to 442.5p. If a restart were fully priced, that sympathy move would have held.
findings.independence: Pause and remaining capacity: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/conduit-holdings-limited-com-shs-di---cre/transaction-in-own-shares/9642908 (30 Jun 2026, last TIOS, 155,754,560 voting rights); https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/conduit-holdings-limited-com-shs-di---cre/holding-s-in-company/9797284 (29 Sep 2026, same base); https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/conduit-holdings-limited-com-shs-di---cre/-50-million-share-buyback-programme/9586141 (26 May 2026, previous programme $47m)

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was a benign cat quarter for London-listed reinsurance peers: Lancashire called it 'relatively benign' with Middle East exposure 'not material', Hiscox said benign cat more than offset Middle East marine losses, and Gallagher Re put 9M insured cat losses at a seven-year low. So Conduit's Q3 underwriting line is likely clean.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Benign Q3 2025: +2.91%. Peers on their own benign Q3 2026 statements: Hiscox +2.97% (3 Nov), Lancashire +1.44% (4 Nov) (Yahoo closes).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: CRE rose 1.1% and 2.7% on the Hiscox and Lancashire days, then gave it back. What is not priced is Conduit's own confirmation, and the 8.5% drop on 2026-10-08 shows the market doubts this name's cat net more than its peers'. So the residual is small.

findings.finding: On 10 Sep 2026 Conduit's own CEO said political-violence losses from the Middle East conflict could reach about $4bn, against Marsh Re's >$2bn. Arch then booked Iran-war claims inside a Q3 cat charge of $234m against $72m a year earlier. Conduit had called its Middle East estimate 'not material' in Q1 and H1, so a Q3 increase is a live downside line, though Hiscox kept its reserve unchanged.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior surprise on this line for CRE. The H1 2026 'not material' statement came with +1.82% on the interims day.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an industry-level remark at Monte Carlo, not a company disclosure, and no sell-side estimate is visible. The short register is covering (1.37% to 1.26%), which is not what an expected reserve hit looks like. This is an inference from an industry number to the company, so it stays small.

findings.finding: Higher government bond yields in Q3 2026 marked down short-duration reinsurance portfolios: Lancashire says Q3 MTM offset its investment income, and its market yield was 5.3% against 4.5% a year earlier. Conduit's 9M investment return will therefore print far below last year's 5.4% (H1 2026 was 0.9%), which hits TNAV growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025's '5.4% strong investment return' headline came with +2.91%; the H1 2026 0.9% return came with +1.82%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because Treasury yields are public. The residual is the year-on-year headline contrast (5.4% last year), which a headline-reading tape may sell briefly.
findings.independence: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/conduit-holdings-limited-com-shs-di---cre/interim-results-for-the-six-months-ended-30-06-26/9692327 (H1 return 0.9%, hit by rising Treasury yields)

findings.finding: CRE fell 8.5% on 2026-10-08 (459p to 420p) as Hurricane Isaias approached the Florida Panhandle; it landed on 9 Oct as a Cat 2 and modellers put insured losses at $1-3bn (Verisk, KCC, Cotality). The Q4 commentary in the release is therefore likely to call it immaterial, which removes the overhang that the incomplete recovery to 442.5p still holds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2024 cat costs of $28.6m ('passed first test'); no measured reaction on a Q4 event comment. The 2026-10-08 move itself was -8.5% on the event alone.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock recovered to 461p by 5 Nov but is back at 442.5p, below the 459p it held before Isaias, so some event premium may remain. Small, because the industry estimates have been public for weeks.

findings.finding: Rates are softening faster into 1/1 2027: Hiscox Re 9M rates are down 14%, property cat was down about 16% at mid-year (Gallagher Re), and Conduit's own RARC went from (5)% in Q1 to (6)% in H1 with property at (10)%. So the release's outlook and 9M RARC will likely read weaker, and GWP will be flat to down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Every 2026 update has flagged softening (Q1 +2.14%, H1 +1.82%), and the stock has not sold off on it.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the softening is a sector-wide narrative and CRE trades below book. The residual is only a worse-than-expected property RARC.

findings.finding: FIL Limited cut its holding from 12.63% to 9.98% in four TR-1 steps between 14 and 29 Sep 2026, mainly by unwinding cash-settled CFDs, so a large holder has been a net seller into strength.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: During the sales the stock ran to 480p on 17 Sep (3.1m shares), then fell back to 442.5p.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed six weeks ago and most likely absorbed. Kept only as residual supply that a buyback restart would meet.

baseline_tension: Agrees with the mild positive priced_lean (+0.99, mostly the short-squeeze component on a 1.26% register that is covering) and runs against nothing in a flat run-up (-0.23% over 20 days). The findings are small and mostly peer-priced, so the scaled number stays modest.
language_note: The domestic RNS record (Investegate) carried two things no English wire or trade-press source did: the frozen share count since 25 Jun 2026 (last Transaction in Own Shares RNS, plus the voting-rights base in FIL's TR-1s) and the remaining-programme arithmetic across three RNSs. It also supplied the issuer's own 07:00 UK release time, and FIL's Sept stake reduction appears only in TR-1s.
Otherwise nothing the English sources did not already carry: the international trade press (Artemis, Business Insurance, Insurance Business) supplied the cat, Isaias and Middle East context.
lessons_applied: Understatement is the hunters' systematic error / size the move on what is new: abs_move_pct raised 3.5 -> 4.0 (the quarter's numbers are new in this release, but no guide is in force, so it stays well below the 7% base).
The decisive company-level fact (buyback restart capacity, about 5% of market cap, from primary RNSs) was sized larger, +0.8 -> +1.0, and not divided down to leave room for the others.
Narrow proxy / macro-to-company transmission: the Middle East and investment-mark findings were kept small and unchanged. They were already sized as proxies, so nothing was applied twice.
